title: Maplecroft Insurance — MLOps handbook (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
Quick working handbook that captures operational decisions and integration gotchas from the Maplecroft Insurance pilot kickoff and subsequent tech syncs. Intended as a single-page runnable checklist for the first two weeks of Dedicated/Private onboarding. Not final — rough notes, assumptions, and open questions at the bottom.

High-level scope:
- Objective: Replace rule-based claims triage with an LLM-backed triage assistant that summarizes incident descriptions, assigns severity codes, and suggests next-step tasks for claims handlers.
- Deployment mode: Private deployment (VPC + on-prem inference nodes in customer datacenter).
- Primary constraints: PHI-equivalent policy, strict egress restrictions (no external model hosting), KMS required for keys, audit logs retained 2 years.

Architecture decisions (working):
1) Model selection: start with open Llama-2-style 13B quantized variant compatible with our runtime. Swap to 70B only if latency SLOs and cost envelope can be met.
2) Inference topology: dedicated private control plane + on-prem serving cluster (4x A100-equivalent nodes) with autoscale window for business hours.
3) KV-cache & prefix caching: enable prefix cache for common claim phrasing to shave tail latency for repeat phrases.
4) Prompting & tool-calling: use structured JSON tool responses to avoid free-text ambiguity. Small function schema for severity mapping and task suggestions.

SLOs and metrics to monitor (initial):
- P95 response latency (first token) <= 220ms for single-request inference on weekday peak.
- End-to-end latency (user sees final suggestion) <= 1.5s for up to 512 input tokens.
- Accuracy target: parity with rule-based triage for severity mapping >= 92% on validation set.
- Token cost estimate: baseline quantized model expected ~0.6x hosted per-token cost due to on-prem throughput optimizations; track closely.

Integration gotchas discovered so far:
- Customer canonicalization: Maplecroft has multiple claim description templates and an archaic HTML blob field; need a robust pre-cleaning step (strip markup + normalize dates/currency).
- Timezones & business hours: claim timestamps stored in legacy offset-less format. Mapping to local business hours is necessary for SLA enforcement.
- KMS key rotation cadence is monthly in their policy; ensure our token cache eviction interacts with rotation window to avoid 401 storms.
- Audit log volume: enabling full request/response audit at 100% will saturate their ELK cluster; propose sampling at 10% + high-fidelity logs for failures.
- Model quantization artifacts: early quantized build produced hallucinated severity scores for edge cases (very short descriptions). Add short-input heuristics to fall back to a deterministic ruleset.

Runbook snippets (first-response ops):
- If node GPU memory crosses 92% for >5m: scale up 1 node and send alert to infra-oncall (Slack #maplecroft-infra).
- If model variance (measured by n-gram disagreement) exceeds threshold for 30m: rollback to previous model build and kick off eval job.
- Key rotation failure: temporarily pause request routing to on-prem cluster, switch to dedicated staging key, and notify security owners.

Security / privacy checklist (must-haves):
- Inbound data: sanitize patient identifiers, hash SSNs before persistence, strip attachments unless approved.
- Network: no outbound to public inference endpoints; egress firewall rules required for control-plane telemetry only (TLS to Redwood control plane on port 443).
- KMS: integrate with customer HSM using PKCS#11; document fallback for HSM maintenance windows.
- Compliance artifact: produce signed attestation for data residency and list of hosts with mounted disks.

Short-term next steps (owner assignments):
- Priya: finalize pre-cleaning pipeline pattern and share sample notebook (due 2026-02-16).
- James O'Neil: hookup KMS integration test with customer's ops team and validate rotation behavior (due 2026-02-18).
- Marta: draft audit log sampling config and ELK ingestion plan with Maplecroft infra (due 2026-02-17).
- Liu Wei: synthetic eval harness for severity mapping + short-input fallback heuristics (due 2026-02-20).

Open questions / risks:
- Business: what is acceptable tail-latency during month-end processing? They indicated "some slowness is OK" but no numeric bound. Need explicit SLA.
- Technical: can their on-prem network sustain periodic model downloads for updates (70B would be ~60–120GB)? If not, we will need a staged delta distribution plan.
- Security: do they require logs to be stored in their S3 equivalent or can Redwood keep ephemeral logs with periodic exports?
- Cost: unknown OPEX model for on-prem GPUs (customer may want to cap monthly VM hours). Need to draft pricing fallbacks for constrained budgets.

Quick experiment ideas to run in pilot week 1:
- Micro-benchmark: run sample claim corpus (5k docs) with and without prefix cache to measure P95 improvements.
- Short-input guard: implement tiny rule-based path for inputs < 30 chars to compare severity accuracy.
- Audit sample: capture 1% of requests end-to-end and verify storage/ingestion pipeline.

Notes to self:
- Keep this page as single source of truth for two weeks; convert to Confluence when core decisions are locked.
- Call notes live in linked JIRA tickets — do cross-link after each sync.

End of draft.
